sections.heading: Rowlatt to Jallianwala — the moral rupture of 1919

blocks.text: The **Rowlatt Act (March 1919)** — 'no dalil, no vakil, no appeal': wartime detention without trial made permanent — betrayed India's war loyalty (13 lakh soldiers, money, men) precisely when reward was expected. Gandhi, fresh from the local satyagrahas (**Champaran 1917 — indigo tinkathia; Kheda 1918 — revenue; Ahmedabad 1918 — mill wages, first hunger strike**), called his **first all-India satyagraha: hartal (6 April 1919)**. Punjab convulsed; on **13 April 1919 (Baisakhi), Brigadier-General Dyer** fired 1,650 rounds into the trapped Jallianwala Bagh crowd — official toll 379 (Congress inquiry ~1,000). The **Hunter Committee's** whitewash and the Lords' celebration of Dyer ('saviour of Punjab', the morning-post purse) — plus **Tagore renouncing his knighthood** — convinced Gandhi the empire was 'satanic'.

rows: Twin grievances + swaraj

**Punjab wrong + Khilafat wrong** (Ottoman Caliphate's dismemberment — Ali brothers' cause) + **Swaraj in one year**; Congress adopted NCM at **Calcutta special session (Sept 1920)**, confirmed **Nagpur (Dec 1920** — Congress constitution rewritten: village-to-AICC structure, 4-anna membership, linguistic PCCs)
Programme
Surrender titles; boycott schools-courts-councils-foreign cloth; **charkha & khadi**; national schools (Jamia Millia, Kashi/Gujarat Vidyapiths); Tilak Swaraj Fund (₹1 crore); no-tax preparedness
Participation

First true mass movement: students (~90,000 left schools), lawyers (Motilal, C.R. Das, Rajendra Prasad quit practice), **women, Muslims (Khilafat fusion — communal unity's high tide)**, peasants (UP kisan link), merchants
Climax & withdrawal

Prince of Wales boycott (Nov 1921); mass arrests (~30,000); **Chauri Chaura (5 Feb 1922** — 22 policemen burnt) → Gandhi withdrew via **Bardoli resolution (12 Feb 1922)**; jailed March 1922 (six years — the 'great trial' speech)

items: **Why withdrawal**: means-ends purity (violence would corrupt swaraj); tactical retreat before state repression could crush an undisciplined mass — criticised bitterly (young Bose/Nehru; 'national calamity' — but the movement had already transformed politics: fear of the Raj broke.

**Aftermath**: Khilafat collapsed (Kemal abolished the Caliphate, 1924); communal riots returned (Moplah 1921's shadow); **Swarajists (C.R. Das-Motilal, 1923)** entered councils to wreck from within vs No-changers' constructive work — the movement's twin heirs.

**Andhra's Non-Cooperation**: coastal Andhra was among the most intense theatres — **Chirala-Perala (1921)**: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led an entire town (~15,000) out to 'Ramnagar' for 11 months against municipal taxation; **Pedanandipadu (Guntur, 1921-22)**: no-tax campaign under Parvataneni Virayya Chowdary nearly stopped revenue collection; **Alluri Sitarama Raju's Rampa rebellion (1922-24)** rose as NCM ebbed (full note in HCOA-065); Konda Venkatappayya, Ayyadevara, Tanguturi Prakasam anchored the Congress machine — Andhra earned its 'frontline province' reputation here.

**Verdict**: NCM failed its one-year promise but achieved the deeper swaraj — **mass fearlessness, Congress as a mass machine, khadi as uniform, Hindu-Muslim unity's best moment** — the template every later movement reused.

items: Date spine: Mar 1919 (Rowlatt), 6 Apr (hartal), 13 Apr (Bagh), Sept/Dec 1920 (Calcutta/Nagpur), Nov 1921 (Prince), 5-12 Feb 1922 (Chauri Chaura-Bardoli).
The Andhra paragraph (Chirala-Perala + Pedanandipadu + Alluri's timing) is APPSC's differentiator — few all-India answers carry it.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Frame NCM as the movement that traded a year's swaraj for a generation's fearlessness. Chauri Chaura questions want the means-ends logic PLUS the criticism PLUS the verdict — all three, briefly.

prelimsPointers: Local satyagrahas: **Champaran 1917 (indigo, tinkathia), Ahmedabad 1918 (first hunger strike), Kheda 1918 (revenue)**.
**Rowlatt Act, March 1919** — detention without trial; only unofficial Indian members' unanimous dissent.
**Jallianwala Bagh: 13 April 1919**; Dyer; **Hunter Committee (1920)**; Tagore renounced knighthood; Udham Singh shot O'Dwyer (1940, London).
NCM adopted: **Calcutta special session Sept 1920 (Lala Lajpat Rai presiding)**; **Nagpur Dec 1920** restructured Congress (linguistic PCCs — Andhra PCC among the first fruits).
**Chauri Chaura: 5 February 1922**; withdrawal by the **Bardoli resolution, 12 February 1922**; Gandhi sentenced to six years (March 1922).
**Chirala-Perala (1921)** — Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya's 11-month town exodus; **Pedanandipadu (Guntur)** no-tax campaign.
**Khilafat Committee (1919, Ali brothers)**; Caliphate abolished by **Kemal Ataturk, 1924**.
Swaraj Party: **C.R. Das & Motilal Nehru, 1923** (after Gaya Congress).
mainsAngles: 1919 was the empire's moral bankruptcy filed in public — analyse Rowlatt-Jallianwala as the hinge of Gandhian nationalism.
Non-Cooperation promised swaraj in a year and delivered fearlessness for a generation — assess.
Was the Khilafat fusion a masterstroke of unity or a mixing of religion and politics with a communal bill? Argue both sides.
Chauri Chaura and the withdrawal: tactical wisdom or national calamity?
Chirala-Perala and Pedanandipadu made Andhra a frontline province — narrate and evaluate Andhra's Non-Cooperation.

glossary.definition: Gandhi's method of truth-force — nonviolent resistance that accepts suffering to convert, not coerce, the opponent.
A general cessation of work and business as political protest — the opening act of the Rowlatt satyagraha.
Indian Muslim campaign (1919-24) to preserve the Ottoman Caliphate — fused by Gandhi with the national cause.
The spinning wheel and hand-woven cloth — Non-Cooperation's economic weapon and moral uniform.
Post-1922 split between constructive-work Gandhians and council-entry wreckers (Das-Motilal) — twin strategies of the lull.
The Champaran obligation to plant indigo on 3/20ths of one's land — the exaction Gandhi's first satyagraha ended.

blocks.text: **Simon Commission (1927, all-white)** → black-flag boycott ('Simon Go Back'; Lala Lajpat Rai's fatal lathi injuries, Lahore) → the **Nehru Report (1928)** (dominion status; Jinnah's rejected Fourteen Points the communal counter) → **Lahore Congress (Dec 1929, Jawaharlal presiding): Purna Swaraj** resolved; **26 January 1930** first Independence Day. Gandhi's **Eleven Demands** ignored → the masterstroke: **salt** — the tax every poorest Indian paid. The **Dandi March: 12 March–6 April 1930, Sabarmati to Dandi, 240 miles, 78 marchers**; salt lifted, the law broken, and the nation followed.

rows: Salt satyagrahas nationwide (**Dharasana raid — Webb Miller's despatches; Vedaranyam — Rajaji's southern march**); no-tax, forest-law breaches, liquor picketing (women's mass entry — Sarojini Naidu at Dharasana); NWFP's **Khudai Khidmatgars (Badshah Khan)**; Nagaland's Rani Gaidinliu; ~90,000 jailed; **First RTC (Nov 1930)** boycotted
**Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 Mar 1931)**

Movement suspended; prisoners released (not Bhagat Singh trio — executed **23 Mar 1931**); coastal salt-making allowed; Gandhi to the **Second RTC (Sept-Dec 1931)** as Congress's sole delegate — wrecked on the minorities question

Willingdon's crackdown (Gandhi arrested Jan 1932); **Communal Award (Aug 1932)** — separate Dalit electorates → Gandhi's Yeravda fast → **Poona Pact (24 Sept 1932)**: joint electorates with reserved seats (148); movement withdrawn 1934; **Third RTC (1932)** Congress-less
Constitutional issue
RTCs + White Paper → **Government of India Act 1935** (see HCOI-096); Congress swept the **1937 provincial elections** — office as the movement's paradoxical dividend

items: **Compared with NCM**: wider geography (villages, princely edges), deeper women's participation, a clear positive act (making salt) vs boycott's negations, but **thinner Muslim participation** (Khilafat's absence; the communal decade beginning) — the standard comparison paragraph.

**The RTC lesson**: London conferences without Congress were theatre; with Congress alone they broke on minority arithmetic the Raj itself had constructed — 'divide and rule' formalised as 'divide and confer'.
**Poona Pact's double edge**: saved joint electorates and multiplied reserved seats, but Ambedkar's assessment — representation without power to choose representatives — feeds directly into HCOI-036.

**Andhra's Civil Disobedience**: salt camps at **Mypadu (Nellore), Chinnapuram/Machilipatnam (Krishna), Vizag coast**; leaders — **T. Prakasam & Konda Venkatappayya** courted arrest at Madras Marina's Vedaranyam-parallel; **Duggirala's heirs** and women (Ponaka Kanakamma — Nellore's satyagraha financier-organiser; Durgabai Deshmukh — the young Kakinada volunteer commanding women's pickets); forest satyagrahas in the agency belts; the **no-tax campaign in Venkatagiri zamindari** — Andhra again among the highest-arrest provinces.

Why salt: universality + legality's absurdity + women's kitchen-politics entry — the three-reason answer to the classic 'why was salt chosen?'

blocks.text: Exam tip: The Mypadu salt camp and Durgabai-Kanakamma women's leadership are Andhra's CDM signatures. On RTCs, one sentence each is enough — the analysis lives in why they failed (minorities arithmetic), not in their proceedings.

prelimsPointers: **Simon Commission announced Nov 1927; landed Feb 1928**; Lala Lajpat Rai died Nov 1928 of lathi injuries.
**Lahore Congress Dec 1929 (Jawaharlal Nehru)** — Purna Swaraj; **26 Jan 1930** observed as Independence Day.
**Dandi March: 12 March–6 April 1930; 78 marchers; ~240 miles (385 km)**; Gandhi arrested 5 May; **Dharasana raid 21 May 1930** (Sarojini Naidu led).
**Vedaranyam march — C. Rajagopalachari (April 1930)**; Andhra's camps: **Mypadu (Nellore), Chinnapuram (Krishna coast)**.
**Gandhi-Irwin Pact: 5 March 1931**; **Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev executed 23 March 1931**; Karachi Congress (1931) — fundamental-rights resolution.
RTCs: **I — Nov 1930 (no Congress); II — Sept-Dec 1931 (Gandhi); III — Nov-Dec 1932 (neither Gandhi nor Congress)**.
**Communal Award 16 Aug 1932 (Ramsay MacDonald)** → **Poona Pact 24 Sept 1932** (148 reserved seats, joint electorates).
**Khudai Khidmatgars ('Red Shirts') — Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**; Peshawar's Garhwal Rifles refused to fire (Apr 1930).
mainsAngles: Why salt? Decode the genius of Dandi as symbol, strategy and mass mobiliser.
Compare Civil Disobedience with Non-Cooperation on aims, breadth and outcomes.
The Round Table Conferences were designed to divide and confer — evaluate their failure and constitutional harvest.
The Poona Pact resolved a fast and opened a debate — examine its terms and Ambedkar's critique.
Reconstruct Andhra's Civil Disobedience through its salt camps, women leaders and no-tax campaigns.

glossary.definition: Complete independence — the Lahore (1929) redefinition of the national goal beyond dominion status.
Gandhi's Jan 1930 minimum programme (salt tax, land revenue cut, prohibition, etc.) whose rejection triggered Dandi.
MacDonald's 1932 grant of separate electorates to minorities including Depressed Classes — reversed for Dalits by the Poona Pact.
Gandhi-Ambedkar agreement (Sept 1932): joint electorates with 148 reserved Dalit seats and primary-election safeguards.
London constitutional negotiations (1930-32) among British parties, princes and Indian delegations — prelude to the 1935 Act.
Badshah Khan's Pashtun nonviolent 'Servants of God' — the frontier's astonishing satyagraha army.

blocks.text: War came without consent (Linlithgow's 1939 declaration → Congress ministries resigned, Oct-Nov 1939; League's 'Deliverance Day'); the **August Offer (1940)** and **individual satyagraha (Vinoba first, Nehru second)** kept protest alive; **Cripps Mission (March-April 1942)** — dominion status post-war, provinces' opt-out — failed ('a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'). With Japan at the door, the **AICC at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, 8 August 1942** passed Quit India; Gandhi's mantra: **'Do or Die' (karenge ya marenge)**. By dawn the leadership was jailed (Gandhi—Aga Khan Palace; Working Committee—Ahmednagar Fort) — and the **leaderless movement** erupted: strikes, sabotaged rails-telegraphs, and **parallel governments** — **Ballia (Chittu Pandey), Tamluk's Jatiya Sarkar (Bengal — Matangini Hazra's martyrdom, Vidyut Vahini), Satara's Prati Sarkar (Nana Patil, ~1943-46)**. Repression was war-grade: ~10,000 dead by unofficial counts, 60,000+ arrests, machine-gunning from the air. **Underground network**: Jayaprakash Narayan (Hazaribagh escape), Aruna Asaf Ali (hoisted the Gowalia flag), Achyut Patwardhan, RS Lohia, **Usha Mehta's Congress Radio**.

rows: Bose's road

Congress president **Haripura 1938, re-elected Tripuri 1939 defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya** ('Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat' — Gandhi) → resigned, founded **Forward Bloc (1939)** → house escape (Jan 1941) → Berlin → submarine to Singapore (1943)
INA

Founded from POWs by **Mohan Singh (1942**, Fujiwara's aid); revived by **Bose (Singapore, July 1943)** — 'Give me blood…'; **Azad Hind Government (21 Oct 1943**, recognised by 9 Axis powers; Andamans renamed Shahid & Swaraj); **Rani of Jhansi Regiment (Lakshmi Swaminathan)**; Imphal-Kohima campaign (1944) — Moirang flag; retreat; Bose's reported air-crash death (**18 Aug 1945, Taipei**)
INA's Indian moment

**Red Fort trials (Nov 1945 — Shah Nawaz, Sahgal, Dhillon; defence: Bhulabhai Desai, Nehru)**: all communities rallied; **RIN ratings' revolt (Feb 1946, Bombay)** — the loyalty of the armed forces visibly cracked: the empire's final calculus changed

items: **Quit India's meaning**: the masses acted without leaders — independence became non-negotiable; but violence-vs-creed debates, League's counter-consolidation (its ministries spread), and Communists' 'People's War' abstention (with the CPI's separate trajectory) complicated the legacy.

**Bose-vs-Gandhi as method, not goal**: armed liberation with Axis help vs nonviolent mass pressure — the honest verdict: the INA failed militarily, succeeded **psychologically** (trials + RIN = the army question), while Quit India proved ungovernability; **1947 = both pressures compounding** on a war-exhausted Britain.

**Andhra 1942**: coastal Andhra's railways-telegraph sabotage (Tenali, Guntur, Bhimavaram belts), student militancy, firings (**Tenali railway station's toll**, Kakinada, Palakollu episodes); underground networks sheltered by delta villages; in the Nizam's Hyderabad the movement was banned but Vande Mataram-era cadres pressed on — Andhra's Quit India casualties place it again among the intense provinces; **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (jailed with the WC at Ahmednagar, co-author of its prison chronicle) is the Andhra name inside the high command.

Parallel-government trio (Ballia-Tamluk-Satara) and the underground quartet (JP-Aruna-Lohia-Usha) are prelims gold; the 'psychological victory' INA verdict is the mains clincher.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Close Quit India-INA answers with the twin-pressure thesis: Gandhi proved India ungovernable; Bose proved the army un-relyable — Attlee's own (reported) admission ranked the INA-RIN factor high. That synthesis is the top-band move.

prelimsPointers: **Quit India resolution: 8 August 1942, Gowalia Tank (August Kranti Maidan)**; 'Do or Die'; leaders arrested 9 Aug (Operation Zero Hour).
Parallel governments: **Ballia (Chittu Pandey, Aug 1942), Tamluk Jatiya Sarkar (Dec 1942-44; Matangini Hazra shot), Satara Prati Sarkar (Nana Patil, longest)**.
**Usha Mehta's Congress Radio (42.34 m)** broadcast till Nov 1942; Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the Gowalia flag.
Bose: president **Haripura 1938**; **defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Tripuri 1939**; **Forward Bloc May 1939**; escape Jan 1941.
**INA**: Mohan Singh (1942) → Bose (Singapore, **July 1943**); **Azad Hind Govt 21 Oct 1943**; Andamans renamed **Shahid & Swaraj**; Moirang flag **14 April 1944**.
**Rani of Jhansi Regiment — Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan (Sahgal)**.
**Red Fort trials Nov 1945** (PK Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan, GS Dhillon); **RIN revolt 18-23 Feb 1946 (HMIS Talwar, Bombay)**.
Cripps offer called **'a post-dated cheque'** (phrase popularly attributed to Gandhi).
mainsAngles: Quit India was a leaderless revolution — analyse its spontaneity, parallel governments and repression.
Explain the failure of the Cripps Mission and its role in precipitating August 1942.
The INA lost its war and won its trial — assess Bose's contribution through the Red Fort and RIN aftermath.
Gandhi and Bose differed on means, not ends — compare their strategies and their compounding effect on 1947.
Document Andhra's Quit India — sabotage, firings and the delta underground — within the all-India storm.

glossary.definition: Gandhi's Quit India mantra — complete freedom or death in its pursuit; the licence for mass initiative once leaders were jailed.
Rebel administrations (Ballia, Tamluk, Satara) running justice, relief and policing where the Raj was expelled in 1942.
The Indian National Army — POW-recruited liberation force revived by Bose under the Provisional Government of Free India (1943).
Courts-martial of INA officers (1945) that united Indian opinion and shook the army's reliability — the empire's endgame accelerant.
The Feb 1946 naval ratings' uprising in Bombay — the clearest signal that armed forces' loyalty had cracked.
1940-41 selected-satyagrahi protest (Vinoba first) asserting free speech against war participation without mass upheaval.
